title: Interpretable Sparsification of Brain Graphs: Better Practices and Effective Designs for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Dense brain graphs create computational costs and reduce model interpretability in graph classification tasks.

gap.claim: Existing noisy-edge selection may not improve performance on sparsified graphs and is often tailored to individual graphs, limiting collective sparsification across multiple graphs.

contributions.claim: The paper investigates GNN designs for sparsifying brain graphs by eliminating noisy edges.

narrative_sequence.summary: Brain graphs are important for neuroscientific and clinical graph classification applications.
Dense brain graphs create computational and interpretability challenges.
The paper investigates GNN designs that sparsify brain graphs by removing noisy edges.
Prior noisy-edge selection may not improve performance and may not generalize across multiple graphs.

source_observation.claim: Sparsification should account for both downstream performance and the ability to apply one selection approach across multiple graphs.

interpretation.claim: An edge-selection criterion based only on explainability or task-irrelevant properties may be insufficient for practical graph sparsification.

application.claim: Evaluate sparsification methods on shared multi-graph settings rather than only on individually tailored graphs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that individually tailored or explainability-based selection is always ineffective.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the proposed GNN designs or edge-selection mechanism.
No datasets, baselines, metrics, quantitative results, or experimental conditions are reported.
The abstract does not establish whether collective sparsification improves performance or interpretability.
